newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-HARDY SCORES TWICE IN DREAM DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HARDY SCORES TWICE IN DREAM DEBUT.

text.p: Winger Mitch Hardy lifted Australia to a convincing 29-15 win against France in the first rugby union test with two tries in a brief but memorable test debut on Saturday.
The ACT Brumbies winger transformed the match during a 12-minute stint during the second half at the Sydney Football Stadium as a temporary replacement for full-back Stephen Larkham.
"First cap and first try for my country -- it was an amazing experience," said Hardy, who was called into the Wallaby squad a week ago as cover for injured first-choice full-back Matthew Burke.
His two tries in the space of three minutes broke a 15-15 deadlock with the Five Nations champions.
But immediately after he scored his second try, Hardy was taken off by Wallaby coach Greg Smith as Larkham had completed treatment for a facial cut.
Both sides scored two tries but Australia captain and lock John Eales contributed 19 points by landing five penalties and two conversions.
"I was very pleased with the performance given that it was our first game this season," Smith said. "To beat France is really special.
"We were having a lot of trouble with our set pieces in the first half and because of that they were putting us under a lot of pressure."
Australia, who scored their opening 15 points through penalties, fully earned the victory with a stirring second half performance after trailing 6-8 at halftime.
Hardy scored his first try when he took a short pass from scrum-half George Gregan before beating two defenders and diving over near the posts in the 68th minute.

Three minutes later, Hardy used his soccer skills to twice kick the ball forward off the ground after a break by right-wing and man-of-the-match Ben Tune, whose performance was rated the best of his test career to date by Smith.
Hardy beat the French defenders in a race to the ball and touched down with his finger tips.
France scored their tries either side of halftime through scintillating breaks from winger Philippe Bernat-Salles and centre Thomas Castaignede.
The second try flowed from one end of the field to the other after fine work by full-back Jean-Luc Sadourny and fly-half David Aucagne.
Centre Richard Dourthe kicked one conversion and one penalty.
"We lost the match in five minutes because of two turnovers," said France coach Jean-Claude Skrela. "In the first half we played quite well and we could have scored one or two tries more."
Assistant coach Pierre Villepreux said: "There was a problem with the number of penalties we gave away. We were caught offside in the ruck and we will have to work on that before the second test.
"But I don't think we are that far behind Australia," he added.
Australia face France in the second and final test in Brisbane on June 28.
Teams:

France - 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Philippe Bernat-Salles, 13-Richard Dourthe, 12-Thomas Castaignede, 11-David Venditti (Sebastien Viars, 39th); 10-David Aucagne, 9-Philippe Carbonneau; 8-Fabien Pelous, 7-Olivier Magne, 6-Abdel Benazzi (captain), 5-Olivier Merle, 4-Olivier Brouzet, 3-Christian Califano, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Franck Tournaire.

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham (16-Mitch Hardy, 59th to 71st); 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-Pat Howard, 11-Joe Roff; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan; 8-Daniel Manu, 7-David Wilson (Troy Coker, 51st), 6-Brett Robinson, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-David Giffen, 3-Ewen McKenzie, 2-Marco Caputo, 1-Richard Harry.
